MARKET.head: California and Pacific Northwest vineyards idle production to cut costs amid weak demand
MARKET.summ: Rather than abandoning vineyards amidst declining demand, some grape growers are pressing pause with the hopes of resuming production in a few years
takeaways: A 2025 study of 19 Willamette Valley vineyards found idling reduced management costs by an average of 38 percent per acre, with some cutting costs in half.
Vineyard idling, a temporary pause in production lasting one to three years, allows producers to avoid removal and preserve assets while awaiting market recovery.
Idled vines require careful management including minimal irrigation, aggressive pruning, weed control, and selective spraying to survive dormancy and resume quality production.

MARKET.head: Early harvests shift wine tourism, logistics, and costs across global regions
MARKET.summ: Along with high temperatures, wine regions around the world reported new records for early grape harvests this summer. For some, it was weeks ahead of the traditional fall schedule, for others it was months in advance. In the heart of the Roussillon in France, Domaine Lafage started picking grapes on July 23, something...
takeaways: Domaine Lafage in Roussillon began harvest on July 23, weeks or months ahead of traditional fall schedules; California's Central Coast started six to eight weeks early, the earliest Kevin Merrill has seen in 27 years.

Wineries face shrinking safe-shipping windows due to heat, delayed payments from fall-delayed sales, rising electricity costs during peak summer demand, and higher insurance and water fees linked to climate pressure.

Wine tourism to hot regions like Paso Robles drops sharply in summer when visitors avoid tasting rooms; European regions like Champagne see tourism extend into November as fall weather improves, offsetting some losses.

MARKET.head: Devastating Spanish wildfires damage 200 hectares in reviving Gredos wine region
MARKET.summ: The ethereal Garnachas of Sierra de Gredos have brought new recognition to this Spanish winemaking region, but after wildfires recently swept through the region, can the momentum continue?
takeaways: Between July 22 and 26, wildfires destroyed 77,000 hectares across Ávila and Madrid provinces; about 200 hectares of vineyard in Cebreros DO, roughly 40 percent of registered area, suffered fire, smoke, or both damage.
Multiple producers including Bodegas Bernabeleva and Bodega El Reventón sustained significant losses: destroyed infrastructure, equipment damage, and uncertain grape yields heading into harvest.

Comando G's slate parcel in Cebreros likely lost its 2024 Las Iruelas bottling to smoke exposure; producers including Daniel Landi and Juanan Martín are drafting proposals to regional authorities for firebreak subsidies and land-clearance support.

MARKET.head: Southern Glazer's pays $12.5 million to settle DOJ bribery investigation
MARKET.summ: On Thursday, alcohol distributor Southern Glazer’s announced that it reached a resolution with the United States Department of Justice (DOJ) and the Alcohol and Tobacco Trade Bureau (TTB) in a longstanding investigation related to improper payments and bribery. In the deal, Southern agreed to pay $12.5 million.
takeaways: Southern Glazer's, the largest alcohol distributor in the US, reached a non-prosecution agreement with the DOJ and Alcohol and Tobacco Trade Bureau on Thursday, resolving a bribery investigation.

From 2016 to 2024, former employees allegedly provided cash, gift cards, luxury goods, golf trips, and resort bookings to retailers in California to secure better shelf placement and other benefits, using false invoices to hide payments.
Beyond the $12.5 million penalty, Southern Glazer's must strengthen compliance and auditing systems over the next two years under obligations not fully disclosed.

MARKET.head: US tariff lift and India trade deal reshape Scotch market in 2026
MARKET.summ: Is it possible that 2026 could eventually be looked back on as the make-or-break year for Scotch whisky? In July, the U.S. finally lifted its 15 month tariff on Scotch, one that had contributed to a 15 percent decline in exports to this country, one of Scotland’s biggest international markets.
takeaways: US lifted its 15-month tariff on Scotch in July 2026, ending a barrier that had cut exports to the country by 15 percent.
UK-India free trade agreement signed in July 2026 aims to open the world's largest whisky market to more affordable Scotch.
Post-pandemic oversupply persists at major distilleries including Diageo and Brown-Forman; some operations like Clynelish closed visitor centers due to weak tourism.

MARKET.head: Trump announces ban on Canadian alcohol imports effective September 29
MARKET.summ: On Tuesday, president Donald Trump announced a plan to ban import of a range of Canadian products, escalating the already tense tariff disputes between the U.S. and its neighbor to the north. The restrictions , which are set to go into effect on Sept.
takeaways: President Donald Trump announced a ban on Canadian imports of wine, spirits, and malt beer, effective September 29, escalating months of tariff disputes.
The ban follows Canada's retaliatory levies on $20 billion of U.S. goods that began after U.S. tariffs took effect on August 22.
Canada's alcohol import ban in 2024 and 2025 significantly reduced U.S. wine, beer, and spirits export revenue.

CULTURE.head: E&J Gallo's Apothic releases blood-bag wine with Heidi Klum for Halloween
CULTURE.summ: The newest trick (and treat) from E&J Gallo’s Apothic Wine is a bloody bag of red wine. Ahead of October, the brand known for inky red blends partnered with queen of Halloween Heidi Klum on a package designed to resemble a blood transfusion bag. Apothic Type ‘A’ Blood Bag dropped online in limited numbers at 10:31 p.m.
takeaways: E&J Gallo's Apothic wine partnered with TV personality Heidi Klum on limited-edition blood-bag packaging dropped online Thursday at 10:31 p.m., priced at $10.31 for two reusable bags in a cooler.
Gallo vice president Marshall Dawson framed the release as a usage vehicle for adult party spaces, targeting Millennials and younger Gen-X consumers who overlap with Klum's Halloween audience.
The campaign coincides with Apothic's rollout of 200-milliliter TetraPak cartons, part of Gallo's broader alternative packaging strategy to recruit new drinkers during the season.

CULTURE.head: Four candidates pass rigorous Master Sommelier exam in Houston
CULTURE.summ: The newest Master Sommeliers share the strategies that helped them prepare for, and ultimately pass, one of the wine industry’s most difficult tests
takeaways: Court of Master Sommeliers, Americas held its final exam rounds September 8-10 in Houston, where 30 candidates sat for the test and only four passed, bringing the global Master Sommelier count to approximately 305.

Alex Mares, wine director at Bourbon Steak New York, scored highest in the cohort after multiple attempts, crediting mental preparation and open-label tasting practice alongside traditional study methods.

Kaysie Rogers at SingleThread Farms in Healdsburg and Steven Washuta of Denver Wine Merchant also passed after multiple attempts, with Rogers and Washuta each emphasizing self-trust and individualized preparation over standardized study approaches.

CULTURE.head: AriZona Iced Tea launches artist residency at New York headquarters
CULTURE.summ: Any marketing executive will tell you that they care about their brand’s aesthetics, but it’s rare to find a corporation where the design language is as distinctive, long-lasting, and personal as AriZona Iced Tea , a commitment that has recently taken an unexpected turn. AriZona Iced Tea entered the market in 1992 with cans...
takeaways: AriZona opened a six-week artist residency program at its Woodbury, New York headquarters, hosting up to four artists per session since July 2025, with three cohorts completed by August.

Residents receive stipends, housing, materials, and access to The Lookout studio and workshop; artists create work inspired by AriZona's Southwest aesthetic and contribute pieces to the company's permanent collection.

The program extends AriZona's 33-year commitment to in-house design and personal creative vision, positioning artistic patronage as a competitive marketing strategy alongside its fixed 99-cent can price.

SCIENCE.head: Seven volcanic wine regions beyond Mount Etna showcase terroir shaped by ancient eruptions
SCIENCE.summ: Mount Etna’s recent eruption reminded the world just how powerful volcanoes can be. For wine lovers, lava flow isn’t something to fear; rather, it’s celebrated as the source of compelling terroir. And while Etna, even when not exploding, often steals the spotlight, other regions around the world boast these unique soils.
takeaways: Volcanic soils from ancient eruptions in Soave, Santorini, the Canary Islands, Hungary, Oregon's Willamette Valley, Auvergne, and California's Lake County create mineral-driven wines with high acidity and savory flavors.
Volcanic terrain offers practical advantages: soils resist pests and disease, enabling organic farming and preservation of old indigenous grape varieties, while protecting vines from harsh climates.

Wine character varies by geology: Soave's Garganega expresses orchard fruit and acidity; Santorini's Assyrtiko delivers mineral depth; Willamette's volcanic Jory soil yields red fruit Pinot Noirs; Lake County's elevation and soils produce tannic, acidic reds.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Highlights: Stesso Stesso Beulah Violetta Rosso 2024 Umbria, Italy
NEWSLETTERS.summ: A lovely low-intervention red from Umbria. Stesso Stesso Beulah Violetta Rosso 2024 Umbria, Italy12.5% alcohol. Stesso Stesso is the winemaking
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Australian couple James Hird and Annie Conley established Stesso Stesso winemaking project at Beulah Violetta, a 150-year-old certified-biodynamic estate near Todi, Umbria.
Stesso Stesso Beulah Violetta Rosso 2024 blends Merlot, Sangiovese, and Sagrantino fermented in stainless steel with minimal sulfite additions.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Heading Out
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Preparing to jump to Italy next week, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker travels to Piemonte's Roero next week for a press tour lasting 9 a.m. to 11 p.m., tasting wines alongside handmade cheese, truffle, hazelnut, and honey.
European wine press tours are funded by EU subsidies and regional consortiums, positioning journalists as products acquired to generate favorable coverage rather than independent guests.
Sarah Marsh MW challenged the Old Vine Conference consensus, noting many old vines carry viruses and young vines can match their quality and resilience to climate extremes.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Myths of The Douro
NEWSLETTERS.summ: If you thought Portugal’s most famous wine region was just heat, heft and port, read on
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Global port wine sales declined 25% over the last two decades; the Douro now produces as much table wine as port, with table wine as the region's economic foundation.

The Douro's strict appellation regulations penalize wines lacking typical 'Douro character' (heavy, high alcohol, oaky), causing innovative producers like Luis Seabra and Rita Marques to declassify wines that don't fit the port-legacy mold.

New-generation winemakers including Dirk Niepoort, Luis Seabra, and Pedro Coelho are producing lighter, higher-altitude Douro table wines with classical structure and acidity, departing from the heavy Parker-style wines that dominated the 2000s.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Drinking Quite Well
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I hope you’ll forgive this column for being somewhat nostalgic. I want to begin by giving a picture of the wine-drinking habits and economics of a particular middle-class English family from the 1960s onwards. I am talking about my own family and you may know from previous articles published here that my father was a
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin's father, a wine merchant, bought Château Lafite 1953 and 1959 for under £2 per bottle in the 1960s; adjusted for inflation, these cost roughly £25 today but now sell for far more.

Top Bordeaux and Burgundy wines affordable to middle-class professionals in the 1960s-1980s are now accessible mainly to plutocrats, a shift driven by increased demand and wealth inequality since the late 1980s.
Atkin personally buys wines in the £12-£30 range and sources quality alternatives from Spain, Argentina, Portugal, Loire, and Southern Rhône rather than expensive cru classé or most Burgundy.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Of Substack & wine
NEWSLETTERS.summ: All that’s being poured for your reading enjoyment in what is currently the most dynamic platform for wine media
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Substack created a Wine & Spirits subsection within its Rising and Top lists, separating wine from the broader Food & Drink category to improve discovery.
Miquel Hudin updated the Wine Substack List (WineStack) with stricter criteria: paid subscriptions must be actively used and content must be text-only, human-written.
Bodhi Landa's 'Thirst Behavior' was removed from WineStack after Substack's AI detection tools confirmed the majority of its text was AI-generated.
